mission: one persistent self.root Frank on accepted Ubuntu VPS, token-addressable by humans/AI bridges, with at most one active execution

findings.result: A parallel frank_spawn_state/frank_spawn_gate implementation was non-admitted: its V15 table was not in the canonical migrator and its runtime directly opened canonical SQLite plus a second long-lived semantic path. The duplicate schema/runtime were removed; canonical V15 presence remains the semantic authority.
findings.negative_result: Do not reintroduce a second spawn-state table/runtime beside frank_presence_lease.

findings.result: V15 heartbeat/release originally checked holder+epoch but not expires_at. An expired holder could renew/release before successor takeover. Runtime now fences expired holder mutations with EXPIRED_LEASE_REQUIRES_RECOVERY; regression test covers pre-takeover and post-takeover stale mutations.

Two-process target-VPS discriminator showed semantic-only V15 can admit successor epoch while old process remains alive/execution-capable after TTL. Linux flock + V15 blocked the live successor; process crash released kernel lock; semantic recovery remained fail-closed until TTL then took over without manual DB repair.

On accepted target VPS, injected +1h wall jump caused premature UTC-only takeover and injected -1h jump delayed recovery. boot_id was present and Python monotonic clock reported monotonic=true, adjustable=false. boot_id+monotonic expiry is a V16 candidate only.
findings.reason: Measured physical one-host lock already closes live-overlap for v0.1; V16 clock complexity requires additional real clock-discipline/reboot benefit evidence.

findings.result: Credential semantics are fused: frank_inbound_token is sole machine-token generation/verification primitive; frank_token_ingress_core performs Bearer/public-error mapping, fixed credential->client/holder binding, scope admission, FrankExecutionGate acquisition, and sanitized FRANK_BUSY. The production network/TLS adapter is intentionally not implemented by stdlib http.server.
open: target-VPS receipt for fused ingress core
production network/TLS adapter and deployment health/recovery
durable execution_id/current-task binding in canonical lease semantics
end-to-end token -> cognition -> response -> release test

keep: UnifiedDB V15 frank_presence_lease as semantic presence authority
Linux FrankExecutionGate physical exclusion on fixed one-host Ubuntu v0.1
frank_inbound_token as sole inbound token credential primitive
reject: direct production FrankPresenceRuntime acquisition outside FrankExecutionGate
stdlib http.server as production internet endpoint
candidate_not_promoted: V16 boot_id + monotonic semantic lease clock

counterhypotheses: Advisory flock is insufficient if any production execution entry path bypasses FrankExecutionGate; static enforcement plus end-to-end entry-path inventory must falsify this.
The extra physical layer could create hung-holder availability loss; cancellation/kill recovery and bounded liveness must be tested before whole-system acceptance.
A fused token core can still be operationally insecure without TLS, ingress rate limits, credential provisioning/rotation deployment and fail-closed server lifecycle.
Persisting execution_id into V16 may be unnecessary if a simpler provenance-bound execution receipt outside lease state proves equivalent; compare before schema growth.
next_falsifiers: obtain fused token ingress target-VPS receipt
inventory all production execution entry paths against static ExecutionGate-only rule
design smallest production TLS/HTTP adapter over fused ingress core using maintained production server stack
run two authenticated-token concurrency test through actual network adapter
test process kill/hang/cancellation and bounded recovery
compare durable execution_id-in-lease vs receipt-bound alternative before any V16 migration
